title: Management approaches to acute muscular strain and hematoma in National level soccer players: a report of two cases.
journal: The Journal of the Canadian Chiropractic Association

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To detail the presentation of two elite female soccer players with right thigh pain that occurred during training. This article will outline the investigation, diagnosis and management of their cases.

sections.label: CLINICAL FEATURES
sections.text: The patients presented with anterior thigh pain following injuries incurred during training camp. Both were diagnosed with acute muscular strain and associated muscular hematomas. The plans of management included rest and removal from sport, cryotherapy, and interferential current. Treatment progressed to soft tissue therapy and rehabilitative exercises. The patient in the first case received additional treatment from another practitioner that involved aggressive soft tissue therapy and a strengthening program in the initial stages of recovery.

sections.label: OUTCOME MEASURES
sections.text: For both athletes, outcome measures included return to play and re-injury.

sections.label: SUMMARY
sections.text: Two female elite soccer players presented with acute muscle strain and hematoma. These case reports attempt to highlight the differences in treatment options in female soccer players.
